title: The health probe interface is elicited from the operator-declared target integration profile; the probe transport, path, response contract, and semantics fall out of that one declaration
context: External supervisors probing a service each carry their own conventions for what a probe looks like and what the answer means. A Kubernetes kubelet expects an HTTPGet, TCPSocket, Exec, or gRPC probe of a specific shape at a container-declared path or port, and reads a two-probe split (liveness vs readiness) as a first-class model. An application load balancer expects one HTTP GET with the answer in the status code and no body semantics beyond that. An uptime monitor expects a URL that returns 200 or 5xx. A systemd unit under `Type=notify` blocks on `sd_notify(READY=1)` and then watches for periodic `WATCHDOG=1` notifications, not synchronous probes. A Docker HEALTHCHECK is an exec command whose exit code is the answer. A service that ships one fixed probe shape is correct for one supervisor and wrong for the others; a service that ships adapter shims per deployment context adds surface area everywhere and never quite matches any convention. The observability-essentials sibling blueprint holds a legitimate different opinion for the case where the service designs its own observability floor without a specific external supervisor's conventions in view: two HTTP JSON probes on the request-traffic listener with a stable body shape, fine when the service is its own supervisor's audience. This blueprint targets the other case: the supervisor's conventions come first and the service materialises the probe surface for them.
decision: The health probe interface is derived from an operator-declared target integration profile. The blueprint ships six profiles: `kubernetes`, `loadBalancer`, `uptimeMonitor`, `systemd`, `dockerHealthcheck`, `reverseProxy`, plus a `custom:<name>` slot for project-authored profiles. Each profile fixes the probe transport (HTTP GET, TCP socket accept, exec command, supervisor notify), the probe path or command surface, the response contract (status code only, minimal JSON body of the shape `{"status":"pass"|"fail"}`, exit code, notify call sequence, or connect-and-close), and the semantic distinction between liveness and readiness (two-endpoint for Kubernetes, single-signal for load balancers and uptime monitors, notify-plus-watchdog for systemd, one-command for Docker HEALTHCHECK). The Kubernetes profile is the shipped default (see ADR-1503). Every HTTP profile carries a `probeListener.separatePort` option for probe traffic isolation (see ADR-1504). The profile object drives every wiring choice; nothing in the process reaches for a probe transport, path, or response outside the profile.
consequences: The probe surface always matches the supervisor conventions the service actually runs under, and a change of supervising system is a configuration change (see REQ-008 and US-14108). Composing this blueprint with the observability-essentials sibling on the same project fires a `healthProbes` global-topic conflict on purpose, because the two blueprints answer different questions about what the probes are for: essentials commits to a self-supervised HTTP JSON contract on the request-traffic listener as the project-wide floor; this blueprint commits to an elicit-and-adapt model whose shape follows the external supervisor. The expected resolution is one project-level ADR that either (a) accepts this blueprint's elicit-and-adapt model when the service must integrate with a specific external supervisor's conventions, (b) accepts observability-essentials's self-supervised fused model when the project designs its own probes without a specific external supervisor's conventions in view, or (c) authors a project-specific hybrid that names both surfaces (e.g., an internal essentials-shaped surface for one audience and a profile-shaped external surface for the supervising system) with explicit boundaries.

alternativesConsidered.name: Fold the elicit-and-adapt shape into observability-essentials as a v2 addition
alternativesConsidered.summary: Extend observability-essentials's ADR-801 to accept a profile-name parameter and let the essentials blueprint carry both the self-supervised default and the external-integration variants inside one contribution set.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The essentials blueprint's identity is the all-in-one basic observability floor (probes plus public status page plus notification outcome sink); merging the elicit-and-adapt shape into it either dilutes that identity or forces the essentials all-in-one bundle onto projects that only wanted the external-integration probe surface. Keeping the two blueprints on separate rows honours the boundary the round-2 canon named and lets each carry the right defaults for its audience.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ship one blueprint per external supervisor
alternativesConsidered.summary: Author `observability-probes-kubernetes`, `observability-probes-load-balancer`, `observability-probes-uptime-monitor`, `observability-probes-systemd`, `observability-probes-docker-healthcheck` as five distinct blueprints, one per supervisor family.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The elicitation surface is small and the profile contract is shared across supervisors; splitting into five blueprints multiplies the maintenance load (five README, five topics.md, five id band allocations, five conflict rows against observability-essentials) without giving the operator anything they cannot express by naming the profile at boot. The single-blueprint form also lets a project that legitimately runs under two supervisors (a Kubernetes deployment fronted by a load balancer whose LB health check hits a different path than the kubelet probes) declare a custom profile that composes the two shapes with one apply.

alternativesConsidered.name: Kubernetes-only blueprint
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship `observability-probes-kubernetes` alone and leave the other supervisors to project-side work or future blueprints.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The round-2 canon explicitly named the identity as `observability-probe-endpoints` (probe endpoints elicited per deployment type; k8s /live /ready default; separate-port/separate-server option), not `observability-probes-kubernetes`. The elicitation is the point; the Kubernetes default is one honoured convention among several the same profile-contract shape covers cleanly.
